contract_plain_english: For floating-point evaluation of the second barycentric quotient with directly computed weights, the paper first gives an exact perturbed numerator/denominator representation with 3n+4 and 3n+2 relative-error counters. It then bounds relative forward error by (3n+4)u times the data condition number plus (3n+2)u times the constant-one, denominator-cancellation condition number, retains O(u^2), and says the bound can be attained within a constant factor. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed expression; PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1 and equations (4.2)-(4.3).)

source_evidence.observation: The inherited setup has n+1 distinct nodes, a fixed evaluation point, exact interpolant p_n=p_f, and cond(x,n,f) defined only when p_n(x) is nonzero.

source_evidence.anchor: Equation (3.2), floating-point model, equation (3.3), and Lemma 3.1
source_evidence.observation: The paper defines w_j as the reciprocal product of x_j-x_k over k != j, assumes the standard relative-error model with unit roundoff u, defines the relative-error counter angle-k, assumes the inputs x_i, f_i, and x are floating-point numbers, and obtains computed weights hat(w_j)=w_j angle-2n_j.
The referenced computation counts subtraction, division, multiplication, and n summation errors; it states that the n-error summation count applies regardless of summation ordering.
The analyzed algorithm is the second or proper barycentric formula: the quotient of sum w_j f_j/(x-x_j) by sum w_j/(x-x_j).

source_evidence.anchor: Exact perturbed numerator/denominator expression preceding Theorem 4.1
source_evidence.observation: The computed quotient is represented exactly first with angle-2n weight errors, angle-(n+3) numerator-evaluation errors, angle-(n+2) denominator-evaluation errors, and an outer angle-1 error, and then with collected angle-(3n+4) numerator and angle-(3n+2) denominator counters.
The first absolute-sum quotient in the forward bound is identified with cond(x,n,f) in barycentric-weight notation.

The theorem gives two first-order forward-error terms with coefficients (3n+4)u and (3n+2)u, retains O(u^2), identifies the terms as cond(x,n,f) and cond(x,n,1), and asserts attainable sharpness within a constant factor.
After the theorem, the paper notes that common rescaling of the weights can be used to avoid overflow and underflow, but this scaling is not part of the displayed Theorem 4.1 computation.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The analyzed variant is specifically the second/proper barycentric quotient (4.1), evaluated in floating-point arithmetic with weights computed from the reciprocal-product formula (3.2); the derivation invokes the same operation counting as Theorem 3.2, including n summation errors regardless of summation ordering. It is not the first/modified Lagrange formula (3.1), and the later optional common rescaling of weights is not incorporated into the displayed model. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: equation (3.2) and Lemma 3.1; PDF p. 4, printed p. 550, anchor: proof of Theorem 3.2; PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: equation (4.1); PDF p. 7, printed p. 553, anchor: weight-rescaling paragraph.)
binders: An interpolation parameter n, n+1 distinct nodes x_j, n+1 data values f_j, and an evaluation point x are in scope, with j=0,...,n. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph.)
The exact barycentric weights are w_j=1/product_{k != j}(x_j-x_k), with interpolation indices inherited as k=0,...,n. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: equation (3.2).)

The exact value is p_n(x), and the computed result of the second barycentric formula is hat(p_n(x)). (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: equation (4.1) and the computed quotient preceding Theorem 4.1.)
The numerical model binds unit roundoff u and local errors delta_i with |delta_i| <= u inside relative-error counters. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: floating-point model and equation (3.3).)
conclusions: The exact finite rounding-error representation is hat(p_n(x))=([sum_{j=0}^n (w_j angle-2n_j/(x-x_j)) f_j angle-(n+3)_j]/[sum_{j=0}^n (w_j angle-2n_j/(x-x_j)) angle-(n+2)_j]) angle-1 = [sum_{j=0}^n (w_j/(x-x_j)) f_j angle-(3n+4)_j]/[sum_{j=0}^n (w_j/(x-x_j)) angle-(3n+2)_j]. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact perturbed numerator/denominator expression preceding Theorem 4.1.)

Theorem 4.1 states |p_n(x)-hat(p_n(x))|/|p_n(x)| <= (3n+4)u [sum_{j=0}^n |w_j f_j/(x-x_j)|]/|sum_{j=0}^n w_j f_j/(x-x_j)| + (3n+2)u [sum_{j=0}^n |w_j/(x-x_j)|]/|sum_{j=0}^n w_j/(x-x_j)| + O(u^2). (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1, first displayed inequality.)

Equation (4.2) rewrites the first term exactly as (3n+4)u cond(x,n,f), while retaining the second denominator-cancellation quotient with coefficient (3n+2)u and retaining O(u^2). (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: equation (4.2).)

Equation (4.3) further rewrites the bound as (3n+4)u cond(x,n,f)+(3n+2)u cond(x,n,1)+O(u^2), where 1 denotes the function whose data values are all exactly one. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: equation (4.3) and following sentence.)
There exist rounding errors for which the Theorem 4.1 bound is attained to within a constant factor. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: sentence following equation (4.3).)
constants_and_indexing: All barycentric sums run over j=0,...,n and contain n+1 terms. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: equation (4.1) and exact computed expression.)

The collected numerator counter is exactly 3n+4 and its first-order coefficient is exactly (3n+4)u. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed expression; PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)

The collected denominator counter is exactly 3n+2 and its first-order coefficient is exactly (3n+2)u. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed expression; PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)

The uncollected expression has angle-2n_j weight errors, angle-(n+3)_j numerator errors, angle-(n+2)_j denominator errors, and one outer angle-1 quotient error. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed expression.)

The index offset reflects n additions for each n+1-term sum together with the counted term operations and weight-computation errors. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 550, anchor: proof of Theorem 3.2; PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed expression.)
definitions_and_conventions: The second or proper barycentric formula is p_n(x)=[sum_{j=0}^n w_j f_j/(x-x_j)]/[sum_{j=0}^n w_j/(x-x_j)]. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: equation (4.1).)
The exact weights are w_j=1/product_{k != j}(x_j-x_k). (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: equation (3.2).)

The paper's angle-k counter denotes product_{i=1}^k (1+delta_i)^(rho_i), where rho_i is +1 or -1 and |delta_i| <= u; a subscript j means the k errors depend on j. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: equation (3.3) and following paragraph.)
The counter satisfies |angle-k - 1| <= gamma_k=ku/(1-ku) under ku<1. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: paragraph following equation (3.3).)
In barycentric notation, cond(x,n,f)=[sum_{j=0}^n |w_j f_j/(x-x_j)|]/|sum_{j=0}^n w_j f_j/(x-x_j)|. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: rewriting of equation (2.2).)

cond(x,n,1) uses the constant-one data/function and equals the denominator-cancellation quotient [sum |w_j/(x-x_j)|]/|sum w_j/(x-x_j)|. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: equation (4.3) and its explanatory sentence.)
error_notions: The exact counter quotient is a finite rounding-error representation with no omitted terms. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact perturbed numerator/denominator expression.)
The theorem's reported error is normwise only in the scalar sense: relative forward error |p_n(x)-hat(p_n(x))|/|p_n(x)|. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)
The first forward-error contribution is proportional to the componentwise data condition number cond(x,n,f). (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: equation (4.2).)
The second contribution is proportional to denominator cancellation, equivalently cond(x,n,1). (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: equations (4.2)-(4.3).)

The paper explicitly says the finite quotient model does not admit a useful backward-error interpretation. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: paragraph immediately after the exact computed expression.)
exceptional_values: The displayed barycentric quotient contains divisions by x-x_j, but the surrounding theorem does not explicitly state x != x_j or provide an evaluation-at-a-node branch. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: equation (4.1) and exact computed expression.)
The relative forward error requires p_n(x) != 0. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1; PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)

The theorem does not explicitly state that the computed denominator is nonzero or separately exclude overflow, underflow, subnormals, infinities, or NaNs; it relies on the stated relative-error model. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: standard floating-point model; PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: computed quotient.)

The paper later observes that weights may be commonly rescaled to avoid overflow and underflow, but that rescaling is not part of Theorem 4.1's displayed computation. (PDF p. 7, printed p. 553, anchor: weight-rescaling paragraph.)
higher_order_terms: The finite angle-counter quotient on PDF page 5 is exact and contains no big-O term. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed expression.)
Every displayed forward-error form in Theorem 4.1 retains an additive O(u^2) term. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1 and equations (4.2)-(4.3).)
The paper does not give an explicit coefficient, sign, or non-asymptotic bound for the O(u^2) remainder in Theorem 4.1. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)
hypotheses: The x_j are distinct and p_n is the degree-at-most-n polynomial interpolating f_j at x_j. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph.)
The inputs x_i, f_i, and x are floating-point numbers. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: paragraph immediately before Lemma 3.1.)
Each arithmetic operation op in {+,-,*,/} obeys fl(a op b)=(a op b)(1+delta)^(+1 or -1), with |delta| <= u. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: standard floating-point model.)
The relative-error-counter estimate uses gamma_k=ku/(1-ku), with ku<1 assumed. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: definition of gamma_k and equation (3.3).)

The derivation incorporates weights computed from equation (3.2), for which hat(w_j)=w_j angle-2n_j. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: Lemma 3.1; PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed quotient.)

The relative forward error and cond(x,n,f) require p_n(x) != 0, inherited from Definition 2.1 and also forced by the denominator |p_n(x)| in Theorem 4.1. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1; PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)
implicit_context: p_n(x) is the exact interpolated value for the given inputs, whereas hat(p_n(x)) is the result of floating-point evaluation including computed-weight errors. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: Lemma 3.1; PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: computed expression.)

The exact finite counter representation precedes and supports the first-order expansion in Theorem 4.1. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed expression; PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)

The first condition-number term measures sensitivity to f, while the second term measures cancellation in the formula's denominator and is independent of f. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: paragraph following Theorem 4.1.)
The theorem inherits fixed interpolation points and fixed x from Section 2; it is not a bound for perturbations of those quantities. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph.)
norms: The theorem uses scalar absolute values; each numerator of a condition quotient is a sum of termwise absolute values, and each denominator is the absolute value of the corresponding exact sum. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)
No vector or function norm appears in Theorem 4.1. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)
numerical_model: The model is fl(a op b)=(a op b)(1+delta)^(+1 or -1), |delta| <= u, for op in {+,-,*,/}, with u the unit roundoff. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: standard floating-point model.)
The inputs x_i, f_i, and x are assumed already to be floating-point numbers. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: paragraph immediately before Lemma 3.1.)

Computed weights contribute angle-2n_j; after all numerator operations and the final quotient error are collected, numerator terms carry angle-(3n+4)_j, while denominator terms carry angle-(3n+2)_j. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: Lemma 3.1; PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed expression.)
The counters are deterministic bounded relative errors; the paper does not impose probabilistic independence. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: equation (3.3) and subscript-j convention.)

undebatable_constraints: The algorithm is the second/proper barycentric quotient (4.1), not the first/modified Lagrange formula. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: equation (4.1).)

The exact finite model must preserve separate perturbed numerator and denominator sums, with collected counters 3n+4 and 3n+2 respectively. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed expression.)
The forward bound has two additive first-order terms, not just cond(x,n,f)u. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)
The first coefficient is (3n+4)u and the second is (3n+2)u. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: equations (4.2)-(4.3).)
The second condition number is cond(x,n,1), where 1 is the constant-one function/data. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: equation (4.3) and following sentence.)
The O(u^2) term may not be silently dropped when reproducing Theorem 4.1. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1 and equations (4.2)-(4.3).)
The theorem's error is relative forward error against the exact p_n(x), so p_n(x) must be nonzero. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1.)
The paper additionally claims existential sharpness within a constant factor. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: sentence following equation (4.3).)
